shell.draftNotice: Test version. This questionnaire is not evaluated yet.
shell.incomplete: You do not have to commit to anything: for every question you can also state that it is still open or that you would rather not answer it. {count} answers are still missing.
shell.submitted: Submitted. Nothing here can be changed from now on.

step1.title: Part one
step1.intro: This is about how you want to work, what you want to achieve and which rules you would like — not about who you are.
step1.note: There are no better or worse answers and no score at the end. The questionnaire saves as you go; you can stop anytime and continue later.

step2.title: Part two: the commitments
step2.intro: Now it is about hours, money and dates. These are commitments, not self-description — which is why they come later.
step2.note: Everything here describes where you stand today. It is not an obligation, and you can change it later.

values.title: Priorities and limits
values.intro: Short situations in which two reasonable concerns collide. You say separately how important each one is to you — both may be very important.
values.note: There is no right choice and no evaluation of your values. The point is to know what you should talk about.
values.concerns: How important is each of these two concerns to you?
values.pathQuestion: Which way would you choose first under these conditions?

missing.heading: Or:
missing.hint: This counts as an answer. It is not a skip.

sourceLanguage: The questions themselves are shown in German. Translating a measurement instrument is not a translation task but a re-validation: an item that reads differently measures something else, and none of the equivalence work has been done. An English version comes after the cognitive interviews, not before.

discussion.mark: I want to talk about this
discussion.markHint: It then goes to the top of your conversation agenda — even if you both answered the same.

report.title: Your answers
report.intro: This is not an assessment of you. It prepares the conversation that still lies ahead.
report.openIntro: This is the most useful part: exactly here is where you would talk.
report.emptyIntro: Once you have filled in the questionnaire, your answers appear here — sorted and without any rating.

compare.title: The two of you
compare.intro: Side by side, not calculated against each other. There is no fit score and no rating here.
compare.cardsIntro: At most four topics per conversation. Everything else is below for reference.
compare.nothingYet: Nothing to discuss yet — or answers are still missing.
compare.agreementHint: You set the amounts and deadlines, not the questionnaire.
compare.question: Question

transition.title: There is a new version of the questionnaire
transition.intro: The questionnaire has been reworked: better questions, separate reasons for leaving something out, and no score at the end. You decide what happens to your existing answers.
transition.reversible: You can change this later. Your old answers are kept either way.

confirmed.keep_previous: Your existing report stays valid. You can answer again at any time.
confirmed.retake: Done — your old answers are kept, and the new questionnaire is waiting.

discovery.title: What matters to you in the search
discovery.intro: You state a wish per topic. This does not produce a fit score — it produces an order that you set yourself.
discovery.orderIntro: Your first topic is looked at first. The second only breaks a tie. Someone who does not fit your most important topic is not lifted by matches further down.
discovery.nothingChosen: No topic chosen yet. Pick what matters to you below.
discovery.verdictTitle: Your search settings, applied to this person
discovery.verdictIntro: In your order. There is deliberately no overall number here.
